items.title: Meta debuts Muse Spark 1.2  and first coding agent as it ramps up competition with OpenAI, Anthropic
items.summary: Meta has debuted its latest AI model and first AI coding agent.

items.title: Could Microsoft, Amazon, or Google Actually Buy Reddit?
items.summary: Reddit sits at the intersection of AI training data, social commerce, and authentic human conversation, making it one of the most strategically valuable assets on the internet right now. But super-voting insiders hold the real power, and the list of buyers capable of clearing that bar is shorter than you might expect.

items.title: Nuclear Utility Constellation Leads Nasdaq 100 After Earnings
items.summary: Nuclear play Constellation Energy jumped about 7% Thursday morning after beating analyst views on earnings and profits.

items.title: Qualcomm’s (QCOM) BMW Deal Adds To A Bigger Diversification Push
items.summary: Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) signed a long-term deal on July 29 to supply chips for BMW’s future digital cockpit and advanced driver-assistance systems through the next decade. The agreement builds on a partnership that already put the Snapdragon Ride Pilot system into BMW’s iX3, and it arrives while investors are still deciding whether Qualcomm’s push beyond smartphones […]

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Accelerate AI Development Further
items.summary: While rival AI leaders push for regulations and safety guardrails, Mark Zuckerberg is making the case that slowing down may be the most dangerous move of all. His latest op-ed challenges the entire premise of AI doomerism in ways that could reshape the debate.

items.title: The Netflix Shock Reveals Which ETF Structure Protects You Better in a Downturn
items.summary: Netflix shares dropped sharply after its Q2 earnings, but three popular ETFs that all hold the stock reacted in surprisingly different ways. The structure of each fund tells you far more about your real risk than the name on the label.

items.title: Alphabet seeks up to $25 billion from its latest bond sale, Bloomberg News reports
items.summary: Alphabet is looking to raise as much as $25 billion from its latest U.S. bond offering, Bloomberg News reported ‌on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter, weeks after the ‌tech giant's 2026 capital spending outlook triggered a steep selloff.  The maturities on the notes range from two to 40 years, Bloomberg reported.  Alphabet did not immediately comment on the ‌size of the offering.

items.title: CoreWeave is Off 20% Over 3 Months: A Prominent Tech Analyst Expects 65% Gains This Cycle
items.summary: CoreWeave has shed a third of its value in three months while its analyst consensus held firm through every dip, and one prominent tech analyst argues the selloff created the exact entry point investors needed.
